featured.title: Hormuz Traffic Falls to Four Vessels
featured.content: Preliminary shipping data shows that only four vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, down from a 10-day average of 18. None of the recorded crossings involved very large crude carriers or LNG tankers. The waterway previously handled around one-fifth of global oil and LNG supplies. Bab el-Mandeb, by comparison, recorded 22 crossings and has remained more active.

articles.title: Hormuz Traffic Drops to Four Recorded Vessels
articles.content: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has fallen to single digits. Reuters reports that four vessels were recorded crossing on Tuesday, compared with a 10-day average of 18. Two were entering and two were leaving. None were very large crude-oil carriers or LNG tankers. Some vessels may not appear in tracking data if their transponders were switched off, so the figure should be treated as preliminary rather than a complete count.

articles.title: Bab el-Mandeb Remains More Active
articles.content: The Bab el-Mandeb Strait recorded 22 ship crossings on Tuesday, only slightly below the 24 recorded the previous day. The figures suggest that shipping through the southern Red Sea route has been more resilient than traffic through Hormuz, although security concerns continue to affect shipping decisions and costs.

articles.title: Oil Eases but Remains Above $100
articles.content: Oil prices eased slightly on Wednesday after US crude inventories rose more than expected. Brent crude fell to around $107.82 a barrel while West Texas Intermediate was around $104.86. The decline came despite continuing concerns about Saudi supply disruption and the wider Middle East conflict. Reuters reported that US crude inventories increased by 7.1 million barrels for the week ending September 11, compared with expectations for a decline.

articles.title: Saudi Pipeline Disruption Keeps Energy Markets on Alert
articles.content: Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline remains affected following an attack. The 1,200-kilometre pipeline can transport around 4 million barrels of crude per day towards the Red Sea, providing an alternative export route when Hormuz shipping is disrupted. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said oil flows could resume within days, although other estimates have suggested repairs could take considerably longer.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Says Houthi Drone Intercepted Near Mecca
articles.content: Saudi Arabia says its air defences intercepted a Houthi drone south of Mecca before it entered restricted airspace over the holy city. Saudi officials described the protection of Mecca as a major security priority. Houthi officials denied targeting the city and rejected the Saudi account. Because the two sides give conflicting accounts, the intended target has not been independently established.

articles.title: Dangote IPO Remains a Major Nigerian Business Story
articles.content: Dangote Petroleum Refinery's initial public offering continues to attract strong attention after opening on Monday. The offer targets about $1.6 billion, with shares priced at ₦525 each. The Financial Times reports that investors can purchase as few as 10 shares, potentially allowing a much wider group of Nigerians to participate in the country's capital market.

articles.title: Investors Warned to Avoid Fake Dangote IPO Platforms
articles.content: The strong public interest surrounding the Dangote IPO has also created opportunities for fraud. Investors should use only authorised subscription channels and verify payment details before transferring money. The Nigerian Securities and Exchange Commission has warned the public about fraudulent websites, social-media advertisements, unsolicited messages and unauthorised agents connected with the offering.

articles.title: Dangote Refinery Expands Role in European Fuel Supply
articles.content: Dangote Refinery is becoming increasingly connected to international energy markets. Reuters reports that the refinery exported around 80,000 barrels per day of jet fuel to Europe during the second quarter of 2026, equivalent to about 13% of the supply shortfall created by disruptions to Middle Eastern fuel exports. Dangote also increased diesel and gasoil exports, supplying markets in West Africa and Europe.

articles.title: Dangote Reports Major First-Half Profit
articles.content: Dangote Refinery reported $1.82 billion in net profit for the first half of 2026 on revenue of more than $13 billion, according to its prospectus, compared with a $476 million loss in the comparable reporting period. The refinery's performance has benefited from strong refining margins and increased demand for exports during the Middle East energy disruption.

articles.title: Europe Watches Nigeria's Growing Fuel Exports
articles.content: The disruption to Middle Eastern fuel supplies has increased the importance of alternative suppliers. Reuters reports that Dangote became Europe's largest supplier of jet fuel among individual countries after increasing exports during the second quarter. The development highlights how Nigeria's refining sector is becoming more closely connected to European energy security.

articles.title: Energy Shock Continues to Threaten Global Costs
articles.content: The Middle East crisis is affecting more than crude oil prices. Prolonged disruption to major shipping and energy routes could increase costs across aviation, transport, manufacturing and food production. At the same time, Wednesday's fall in oil prices shows that markets are responding to several factors, including US inventories and expectations about the eventual return of disrupted supplies.

articles.title: AI Investment Debate Continues Across Global Markets
articles.content: Artificial intelligence remains a major focus for investors and technology companies. Markets are weighing the potential economic benefits of increasingly capable AI systems against questions surrounding regulation, safety and the enormous cost of building computing infrastructure. AI-related concerns are contributing to a cautious mood in global equity markets alongside geopolitical and energy risks.

articles.title: Asian Markets Remain Cautious Ahead of Fed Decision
articles.content: Asian markets remained cautious on Wednesday as investors assessed oil prices, rising bond yields and the US Federal Reserve's upcoming policy decision. Reuters reported that the US 10-year Treasury yield briefly moved above 5%, while investors continued to monitor geopolitical developments and the debate over the pace of AI investment.

morningSummary: Good morning. The global energy crisis remains at the centre of attention after only four vessels were recorded crossing the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, far below the 10-day average of 18. None of the recorded crossings involved very large crude carriers or LNG tankers. Bab el-Mandeb remained more active, with 22 crossings. Oil prices eased slightly after a larger-than-expected US inventory build but remained above $100. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline continues to face disruption, while Saudi authorities say a Houthi drone was intercepted near Mecca. In Nigeria, the Dangote IPO remains a major business story, while the refinery is also increasing fuel exports to Europe during the global energy disruption.
bigQuestion: With Hormuz traffic falling to just four recorded vessels in one day, how long can the global economy absorb the pressure before consumers begin to feel the effects in everyday life?
